heroTitle: Wildfire damage restoration in Southern California
heroAccent: smoke, soot, ash, and structural response
heroIntro: Wildfire leaves two categories of damage: the obvious structural destruction of a direct burn, and the less visible—but still serious—smoke and ash intrusion that affects homes miles from the fire line. Gallagher Restoration Co. handles both across five Southern California counties, from first call through complete reconstruction.

whatItIs.heading: What does wildfire damage restoration involve?
whatItIs.body: Wildfire damage restoration addresses the full spectrum of harm a fire event causes—whether a home burned directly or simply sat downwind of a major fire for days. For homes with structural fire involvement, restoration follows the same path as fire damage restoration: debris removal, structural assessment, smoke and soot remediation, and full reconstruction. For the larger number of homes that survived the fire but absorbed smoke and ash, restoration focuses on surface decontamination, HVAC system cleaning, content restoration, and air quality verification using HEPA filtration and hydroxyl generators. Ash and wildfire smoke carry compounds—volatile organic compounds, heavy metals from burned structures—that are distinct from typical interior fire residue and require specific treatment protocols. The January 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires created exactly this two-track demand across the greater Los Angeles area: a smaller number of total-loss or heavily damaged homes alongside thousands of properties that need professional remediation, not a garden hose.

process.heading: How Gallagher handles wildfire damage restoration

steps.title: Emergency assessment and safety clearance
steps.body: A real person answers at any hour. The crew arrives—typically within 60 minutes—and documents the full scope: structural integrity, smoke and soot distribution, HVAC contamination, exterior ash load, and contents condition. No work begins before the structure is confirmed safe to enter.

steps.title: Containment and exterior ash removal
steps.body: Exterior surfaces—rooflines, gutters, decking, HVAC intake vents—are cleared of ash before it migrates indoors. Containment barriers prevent cross-contamination between affected and unaffected areas. HVAC systems are shut down and isolated to stop circulating smoke particles.

steps.title: Smoke, soot, and odor remediation
steps.body: IICRC-trained technicians apply appropriate cleaning methods per surface type—dry sponge for light soot, wet chemical cleaning for heavier deposits, thermal fogging and hydroxyl generation for odor neutralization. HEPA air scrubbers run continuously through this phase and are not removed until air-quality readings confirm clearance.

steps.title: Reconstruction and insurance documentation
steps.body: For structurally damaged homes, Gallagher transitions directly into rebuild—framing, drywall, insulation, flooring, cabinetry, paint, and fixtures—under one project management point of contact. Insurance documentation is built from day one: photo logs, moisture and air-quality readings, and line-item scope for the adjuster.

signs.heading: Signs your home needs wildfire damage restoration
signs.intro: Your home does not need to have burned to require professional remediation. These are the conditions that warrant a call.

items.title: Persistent smoke odor after windows are opened
items.body: If the smell does not clear within a few days of the fire passing, smoke compounds have penetrated porous surfaces—drywall, insulation, fabric, wood framing. Ventilation alone will not remove them.

items.title: Visible ash or soot on interior surfaces
items.body: Ash that entered through gaps around windows, doors, or HVAC systems carries toxic compounds from burned structures. Standard cleaning disperses fine particles rather than removing them; HEPA-equipped equipment is required.

items.title: HVAC system ran during or after the fire
items.body: Any system that operated while airborne ash or smoke was present has pulled contaminated air through the ductwork. The entire system—supply lines, return lines, filter housing, and air handler—must be inspected and cleaned before the system runs again.

items.title: Exterior char, melted materials, or structural damage
items.body: Visible burn damage to siding, roof decking, eaves, or framing indicates the fire reached the structure. A professional structural assessment is needed before any interior restoration work begins.

items.title: Unexplained respiratory irritation or headaches indoors
items.body: Wildfire smoke contains fine particulates and chemical compounds that are not visible to the eye. Symptoms that improve when you leave the home are a reliable indicator of indoor air-quality problems requiring professional assessment.

pricing.heading: Wildfire damage restoration pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Wildfire restoration costs vary significantly based on whether the home has structural fire damage or smoke-only intrusion. Smoke and ash remediation for a home that survived the fire but absorbed significant smoke—including HVAC cleaning and air-quality verification—typically falls in the $1,500–$10,000 range depending on square footage and severity of contamination. Structurally damaged homes involving partial or complete reconstruction can run $15,000 to $50,000 or more, with total-loss rebuilds exceeding that range considerably. Every job starts with a free on-site assessment—no charge to arrive, document, and give you an honest scope. Gallagher Restoration Co. coordinates directly with your insurance carrier and builds the line-item documentation package the adjuster requires. Do not sign restoration contracts until you have that free assessment in hand.

faqs.q: My home did not burn, but it smells like smoke. Do I need professional remediation?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Wildfire smoke contains fine particulates and chemical compounds that bind to porous surfaces—drywall, insulation, wood, upholstery. Standard cleaning and ventilation redistribute these particles without removing them. HEPA air scrubbers, appropriate chemical cleaning agents, and odor neutralization equipment are required to bring levels down to safe, clearance-level readings.

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover wildfire smoke damage in California?
faqs.a: Standard homeowners policies in California generally cover wildfire damage, including smoke and soot intrusion to homes that did not burn directly. Coverage specifics depend on your policy. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents cause and scope from day one and coordinates directly with your adjuster to support the claim.

faqs.q: How long does wildfire smoke remediation take?
faqs.a: Smoke-only remediation in a typical Southern California home typically takes three to seven days, depending on the severity of contamination, square footage, and how many surfaces require treatment. HVAC cleaning adds time. Structural restoration timelines vary widely based on the extent of fire damage and reconstruction scope.

faqs.q: Is it safe to stay in a home with wildfire smoke odor?
faqs.a: Persistent wildfire smoke odor indoors indicates elevated fine-particulate and chemical compound levels that can cause respiratory irritation and longer-term health effects, particularly in children and people with existing conditions. Gallagher Restoration Co. recommends temporarily vacating while HEPA scrubbers run and remediation is underway.
